# Generalisation to the Live Final

How well the agent on `steffen/price-engine` (commit `9182604`) should carry over to Sunday: new
suppliers, up to a third of cases mixing supplier and case types practice never showed, some
citing the 08:00 release. Research on Saturday 10 October, evening: the kit's code, all 21 case
files, `logs/runs/`, `exports/`, the data package, and our agent on `arena-sim`. No practice
quota spent. Same conventions as `learnings.md`: date, tag, finding, evidence, consequence.

## Verdict

The code runs on every case structure we know. Its tuning is in-sample and unmeasured beyond
the ten hosted cases. The biggest gaps for Sunday: new suppliers get a neutral profile because
the release's letters and news never reach the persona code; one exception loses a whole case
(or every later wave); four or more bidders time out.

| # | Risk | Damage | Fix | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | an exception in a move or the wave poll | a case at its alternative (0 in 6 of 21), or all later waves | catch per move, keep polling | small |
| 2 | release rows invisible to SQL; most suppliers without text | neutral profile for new suppliers | read release rows via the ID index; scan the supplier's e-mails | small to medium |
| 3 | 4 or more bidders | timeouts, lost patience, ended threads | stop sending to the worst bidders after round 1 | medium, a tactics decision |
| 4 | missed phrasings in `SIGNALS` | traits not detected | widen to word stems | small |
| 5 | `price_unit` ignored | wrong-direction rival or order-price claims | divide by `price_unit` | small |

## Findings

### Robustness

- 2026-10-10 `rules` **Every known case structure runs end to end.** All 21 public case files,
  including the nine never hosted (P06, P09, P12 to P17, P19), played through `arena-sim`
  in-process with our agent and the package, no model: no exception, 0 to 1 s per case. Covers
  bundles (P07 4 parts, P15 3), the 3-bidder RFQ, `tooling_eur` (P06) and up to 75 term
  combinations (P09). The sim's supplier is a fixed script, so this checks code paths, not
  tactics. → Worth a test in `tests/` that plays every case file from `GET /v1/cases` this way
  (load them into `Sim(cases, pkg.facts)`, strip the `hosted` key).
- 2026-10-10 `rules` **One exception loses a case.** `play_case` has no guard around
  `Negotiator.setup` or `move`. Fields a hidden case may lack crash it: a rival quote without
  `unit_price` (`claims.py` `rival_quote`), an index clause without `material_share`
  (`writer.py` `FIELDS`), a scorecard without `quarter` (`claims.py` `scorecard`), a month not in
  `YYYY-MM` (`months_back`). The session then sits until the wave cap, which scores the
  alternative (0 in D01, P05, P06, P10, P14, P17). → Catch per move; on error send our last
  sheet again with the template e-mail.
- 2026-10-10 `rules` **One error stops the final.** `runner.play_waves` re-raises any non-403
  `ArenaError` from the case-list poll, and a network error after the client's retries is not
  caught at all (`arena_kit/client.py` `_call`). Every later wave is then lost; no human may
  restart. → Catch everything in the poll loop, log, sleep, poll again; a crashed case resumes
  with `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}` (a second `POST` is a 409 naming the session).

### Timing

- 2026-10-10 `rules` **Four bidders or more time out.** The arena answers one call per session at
  a time (`arena_kit/client.py`: "a call may wait for another call on the same session first").
  Supplier replies took 19 s median, 28 s p90 (121 moves in `logs/runs/`); our writer 1.8 s
  median, 6.3 s max (73 calls, none failed, 7 dropped by the filter). A thread waits about
  (N - 1) x 21 s for its next message against a 60 s limit:

  | Bidders | Wait at median | Wait at p90 | Rounds per thread in 390 s |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 2 | 23 s | 34 s | 9 / 6 |
  | 3 | 44 s | 66 s, late | 6 / 4 |
  | 4 | 65 s, late | late | 5 / 3 |

  P05 (3 bidders) had one late move in v5. No case file has more than 3 bidders, but hidden
  cases bring "new settings". → With 4 or more bidders, stop sending to the clearly worst ones
  after round 1; the writer's 20 s timeout matters little next to the supplier's reply time.

### Data and the Sunday release

- 2026-10-10 `rules` **The release reaches only part of the agent.** `DataPackage` finds
  `data/release-sunday/` next to the package, merges its `facts.json` (new IDs only) and puts its
  `data/*.csv` rows into the ID index for `lookup` and `ids`, never into SQLite
  (`arena_kit/data.py`, `_ids`). `personas.profile()`, `Negotiator.full_cost()` and the claims
  built from SQL (`po_lines`, `cost_drivers`, `documents`, `suppliers`) never see release rows,
  and document files resolve against the package root, not the release. Release IDs can still be
  cited. `design.md` says the release is "read at runtime"; that holds for `facts.json` only.
  → Read release rows through `pkg.ids(prefix)` / `pkg.lookup` (each row carries `root`) in
  `profile()` and the document claims. Check the CSV schema at 08:00.
- 2026-10-10 `data` **Most suppliers have no text.** Of 447 suppliers, 46 have documents, 31 news,
  18 quote remarks; the other 401 get the neutral profile (rate 7 %, no signals). A new supplier
  in the final is one of them or unknown to the package. → Its own e-mails and the release are
  the only persona source.
- 2026-10-10 `data` 15 of 108 quotes are priced per 100 (13) or per 1000 (2) pieces
  (`quotes.price_unit`). Rival-quote and order-history claims compare `unit_price` with the
  supplier's per-piece price without converting. → Divide by `price_unit` before comparing.
- 2026-10-10 `rules` **Structures only in unplayed cases** (case files): `tooling_eur` negotiable
  and lead time at most 84 days (P06), chargeback in the alternative (P12), index series PPI-C241
  in a clause (P16), fixed payment in a quality case (P12), a 3-part bundle (P15). Every case type
  and category goal appears in at least one hosted case. Only `incoterm` (D02) lies outside the
  fields the planner knows.

### Persona signals

- 2026-10-10 `data` **The patterns are not fitted to the practice suppliers**: the package's text
  is generated and its phrases recur, so all 10 suppliers of the unplayed cases get at least one
  trait. They miss other forms of the same phrases: "restructuring programme with its banks"
  (sup:70150), "negotiating with its banks" (sup:70280), "lowered its rating" (sup:70310),
  "bought their nickel and alloys forward" (sup:70730), "advertising free machine capacity"
  (sup:70250), "allocated in line with last year's call-offs" (sup:70410). "I cannot sign
  anything that lowers our margin now" (5 call notes) is a trait with no pattern. → Widen to word
  stems before the release adds new wording.
- 2026-10-10 `arena` **Supplier e-mails carry traits too:** 13 of 220 supplier e-mails in
  `exports/messages.jsonl` match `SIGNALS` (price_frozen sup:70530; spare_capacity sup:70210,
  70250, DEMO-J1; capacity_full sup:70240; cash_need sup:70210), including a sandbox supplier the
  package does not know. → Scanning each reply gives unknown suppliers a profile (untested in
  play).

### Tuning

- 2026-10-10 `arena` **Out-of-sample performance is unmeasured.** The 0.727 mean is in-sample:
  every constant was tuned on the same ten hosted cases and the other nine cannot be played.
  Runs of one case spread widely across v1 to v6 (P18 0.25 to 0.49 over seven runs, P08 0.40 to
  0.55), and with a model-written paragraph the wording changes per run while wording moves the
  price (`learnings.md`, takeaway 3). → Treat single-run moves below about 0.1 as noise.
- 2026-10-10 `rules` **Evidence behind each constant** in `buyer/policy.py` (from `git log -p`):

  | Constant | Cases behind it | Risk |
  |---|---|---|
  | `ANCHOR` leverage 0.78 | P05, P08 / P18 (one template) | medium |
  | `ANCHOR` routine 0.82 | P07 (P04 overridden by price_frozen) | medium to high |
  | `ANCHOR` quality_first 0.88 | P11 | medium |
  | `ANCHOR` stabilise 0.92, secure_supply 0.88 | none: always overridden in practice | high, untested |
  | `FRACTION` 0.3 | D01, D02, all hosted cases | low |
  | `DEEP` 0.06 | P05 (two job shops), D02 | medium |
  | price_frozen 0.95 | P03, P04 | low to medium |
  | capacity_full 0.93, budget 0.16, overtime 0.005 | P10, P05 sup:70240 | medium |
  | `near_cost` 0.97, budget 0.14 | P02 | high |

  → A hidden `stabilise` or `secure_supply` case with no override opens at an anchor never played.

## Sunday 08:00 checklist

1. `uv run arena data`; confirm `DataPackage("data/package").release` is not `None`.
2. List the release's `data/*.csv` and their columns; count supplier IDs new vs in the package.
3. Run every case file through `arena-sim` again with the release loaded.
# Negotiation strategies: research for our buyer agent

Research report, 10 October 2026. Two inputs: (1) the literature on automated negotiation,
bargaining, procurement practice and LLM negotiators, gathered by ten parallel research agents;
(2) our own 62 logged practice sessions (`logs/sessions/`), read again to see which of those ideas
fit the arena's supplier bots. Each recommendation says what supports it and how to test it. Most
literature points were read from abstracts and summaries, not full papers: treat effect sizes as
directional (sources and confidence at the end).

## Summary

The current price engine scores a mean of **0.73** over the ten hosted cases (best run per case).
The gaps that remain are concentrated: P10 (0.68, 194k EUR from C_best), P08 (0.55, 79k), P18
(0.49, 37k), P11 (0.71, 28k), P07 (0.75, 23k), P02 (0.51, 23k).

What the traces show about the bots, in literature terms: a **behaviour-dependent conceder**
(Faratin, Sierra and Jennings' tactic family) that answers each of our steps with a smaller step
of its own, becomes a little more generous late, and ends the dance with `final_offer` once its
patience is used up. It ends the dance after 2 to 6 of our messages, so the 10-message limit
never binds. **The first counter decides most of the deal.**

Recommendations, ranked by expected gain against cost to build:

| # | Change | Why | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Make round 1 count:** three equal-C sheets (MESO), the strongest claims, a precise anchor with a reason | the first counter holds 40 to 100 % of our final price cut; MESOs anchor harder and reveal priorities | sandbox D01/D02, then P07, P08, P18 |
| 2 | **Answer the supplier's stated need every message**, also when the term is fixed | P11 Kalwisz asked for faster payment five times ("you haven't addressed this at all"), then stopped at 45.50 | P11 replay |
| 3 | **Concede in currencies, not price:** hold one or two terms it values back from round 1 and spend one per round as our move | concessions are only answered after a move; logrolling moves price without paying price | sandbox, then P07 / P08 |
| 4 | **Spend patience in fewer, larger steps** | the bot gives back only 0.2 to 0.7 of each step and stops on a cumulative gap; many small steps burn patience without buying price | sweep `FRACTION` 0.3 / 0.5 / 0.7 on the sandbox (free) |
| 5 | **Expected-value acceptance after `final_offer`** | pushing after `final_offer` walked once (D01); the gain from one more step is small | already behind `BUYER_PUSH_FINAL`; decide from data |
| 6 | **Persona playbook** (table below): the right currency per supplier type | procurement practice and our persona signals agree | per case, one change per batch |
| 7 | **Writing rules for LLM counterparts:** warm, questions, reasons, trades, a story for the boss | largest LLM negotiation study: warmth and questions close deals, dominance causes impasses | wording only; check replies' back office |

What not to do: extreme anchors (walk-aways roughly triple), threats and dominance, bluffed
urgency or rivals, repeating an unchanged sheet, and anything that targets the bot's prompt
(prompt injection is an attack under the rules).

## 1. How the arena's suppliers concede

From the price paths of every logged thread (script logic: supplier price per reply, our price per
message, statuses). Values for the current engine's practice runs:

| Case | Supplier type | Anchor below quote | Its first move | Its step per our step (ρ) | Σ gap at `final_offer` | Deal below quote | Score |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| P07 | routine, family | 18 to 19 % | 2.6 to 3.5 % | 0.3 to 0.7 | 0.12 to 0.19 | 5.6 to 6.8 % | 0.73 to 0.75 |
| P08 | leverage, distributor | 21 % | 8 to 10 % | 0 to 1.0 | 0.09 to 0.23 | 7.3 to 11.6 % | 0.40 to 0.55 |
| P18 | leverage, distributor | 22 % (7 % once) | 7 to 10 % | 0 to 0.9 | 0.09 to 0.14 | 8.2 to 13.1 % | 0.25 to 0.49 |
| P01 | stabilise, price increase | 9 % | 2.4 to 3.5 % | 0.4 to 0.9, then 2 | 0.08 to 0.10 | 5.2 to 6.0 % | 0.90 to 0.97 |
| P11 | quality first, cash short | 12 % | 0 to 2 % | 0.3 to 0.6, then 0 | 0.15 to 0.18 | 3.2 % | 0.71 |
| P10 | secure supply, fully booked | 7 % | 1.6 % | 0.1 to 0.2 | 0.015 | 1.9 to 2.2 % | 0.67 to 0.68 |
| P02 | stabilise, near cost | 5 % (7 % walked) | -0.7 % | 0.05 to 0.4 | 0.03 | about 0 % | 0.46 to 0.51 |
| P03, P04 | price frozen | 4 % | 0.4 to 1.4 % | 0 | 0.04 to 0.06 | 0.4 to 1.4 % | 0.86 to 0.92 |

Findings:

1. **The first counter carries the deal.** In P08 and P18 its first counter already holds 75 to
   100 % of the final cut, in P07 and P01 about half. Later rounds add 0 to 4 points of the quote.
2. **It answers our steps at ρ < 1.** If we close the gap fully, the deal lands at
   `c1 - ρ / (1 + ρ) * (c1 - anchor)`: with ρ = 0.4 at 71 % of the way from our anchor to its first
   counter. Observed: 73 to 90 %, because `final_offer` usually comes before the gap closes.
3. **ρ grows late** (D01: 0.2 early, 1 to 2 in the last rounds), the time-dependent part of the
   tactic. `final_offer` cuts this off before we reach it.
4. **`final_offer` arrives early:** after 2 to 6 of our messages, at a cumulative gap of 0.09 to
   0.23 of its price (0.015 for the fully booked P10). The round limit never binds. The traces
   cannot yet separate a patience budget from a floor that our claims move (the same supplier
   stopped at 5.35 to 5.61 in P08 depending on our path, which points to patience).
5. **A shallow anchor gives a shallow first counter:** P18 opened at 7 % below and got 6.6 %, the
   worst run (0.25); at 22 % below it got 8 to 10 %.
6. **Pushing past `final_offer` risks the deal:** D01 walked away after one more sheet below its
   final (`D01_212404b7930bfc68`).

Consequences: the literature's default against unknown opponents (Boulware, hold early, concede
late) assumes the opponent keeps playing to the deadline. Ours does not, so its advice inverts:
win in round 1, then close the gap in few, deliberate steps before patience runs out.

## 2. Opening and anchoring

**Research.** The first offer anchors the settlement (Galinsky and Mussweiler 2001; NegotiationArena
found opening offers correlate with final prices, rho about 0.72, for LLM agents too). Precise
numbers anchor harder than round ones and signal preparation (Mason et al. 2013; Loschelder et al.
2017). Extreme offers backfire: 30 % walk-aways after an extreme opening against 11 % after a
moderate one (Schweinsberg et al. 2012), confirmed in a 2018 replication. The anchor loses power
when the recipient focuses on its own alternatives and target (Galinsky and Mussweiler).

**For us.**
- Keep the goal-based anchors (`ANCHOR` in `buyer/policy.py`: 0.78 leverage to 0.92 stabilise);
  they sit at the edge the research and our 20 vs 30 % sandbox test agree on. Never above 25 %
  below the quote.
- Make the anchor precise (4.76, not 4.75) and give it one reason the supplier can check: its own
  past price, a falling driver, a rival offer. Already true for the figures; keep the reason next
  to the price in the e-mail.
- Do not open shallow out of politeness: P18 at 7 % below was the worst run.

## 3. Multi-issue offers: MESOs and logrolling

**Research.** Multiple equivalent simultaneous offers (Leonardelli, Gu, McRuer, Medvec and
Galinsky 2019, six experiments) give stronger anchors, better outcomes for the offerer, more joint
gain and a friendlier relationship than one package; recipients read them as sincere. Guidance:
three offers, equal value to us, different mixes, all at or better than our target; the choice
reveals the counterpart's priorities. Automated negotiation does the same on iso-utility curves:
offer packages of equal own value and pick the one closest to the opponent's last offer (Faratin,
Sierra and Jennings 2002; Lai and Sycara). Package deals ("nothing agreed until everything is
agreed") turn a price fight into trades.

**For us.** The arena allows three sheets per message and the bot picks one and answers it
(`learnings.md`). Today we send one sheet per message.

- **Round 1: three sheets of equal C**, each at the anchor's C, varying the terms where the
  supplier's value differs from ours: payment days (its cost of money), contract length, lead
  time, ppm headroom, start date. `eco.plan_terms` already ranks term sets; take the best three
  distinct ones and set each price so C is equal.
- **Read the pick:** the chosen sheet tells us its priority; carry those terms forward (`adopt`
  already takes over terms from its counters).
- **Later rounds:** one sheet is enough unless a new lever opened. A second sheet that trades a
  term for price on its preferred axis is cheap information.
- Hold the walk-away and must-haves on every sheet: three sheets mean three chances for it to
  agree, so each one must be a deal we want (an `agreed` freezes the price).

## 4. Conceding: currency, size and pace

**Research.** ANAC winners pair a tough bidding curve with an opponent model and a lenient
acceptance near the deadline (Baarslag et al.; Fawkes 2013; Agent K 2010 extrapolates the opponent
from the mean and spread of its offers). Shrinking concessions make the counterpart expect a limit
and counter less ambitiously (Tey, Schaerer, Madan and Swaab 2021, seven studies). Deadline
research: agreements cluster at the deadline (Roth, Murnighan and Schoumaker 1988), but here the
supplier's own patience is the effective deadline. Procurement practice: never give a concession
without asking for something specific in return.

**For us.**
- **Concede in currencies the supplier values and we do not.** The bot gives nothing without a
  move from us; a move need not be price. Candidates by case, priced with `total_cost` and its
  `supplier_value`: a 24-month term where it is free to us (P03, P04, P07, P10), forecast and
  volume statements, ppm headroom below the must-have (P11: 300 ppm costs us about 7 EUR per ppm
  point a year; 1000 ppm would cost about 0.31 EUR per unit, which the supplier may value more),
  a later start where we are indifferent, faster payment only for suppliers whose rate exceeds
  our 8 %. Today `plan_terms` gives all of these in round 1. Hold back one or two and release
  one per round as the move, with the price step smaller or zero. Hypothesis: same final price
  with less patience spent.
- **Fewer, larger price steps.** With ρ between 0.2 and 0.7 and a cumulative-gap stop, our
  `FRACTION = 0.3` closes the gap slowly and pays patience for every open round. Sweep 0.3 / 0.5 /
  0.7 on the sandbox, which costs no quota.
- **Shrink our steps visibly** (Tey et al.): the supplier reads them as our limit. Our steps
  already shrink; keep it, and say in words which step is the last.
- **Never move on a round where it did not move**, except with a currency (holding is free; an
  unchanged sheet is "My call: hold" for both sides).

## 5. Acceptance and the end of a thread

**Research.** The standard rule is AC_next: accept when its offer is at least as good as what we
would send next (most common in ANAC, Baarslag et al.); winners add a time rule that relaxes near
the deadline. Bargaining theory gives the expected-value form: accept now when
`C_now <= (1 - p) * E[C_next] + p * C_alt`, with p the chance the next push ends the thread.

**For us.**
- AC_next is in place (`theirs <= ours[-1]` accepts). Keep it.
- After `final_offer`, p is high (one walk in our pushes so far) and the expected gain of one more
  step is small (0 to 1 % in our traces). Accept unless `BUYER_PUSH_FINAL` data shows a net gain
  across several cases; in cases without an alternative (D01, P05, P06, P10, P14, P17) never push.
- Prepare the worst acceptable sheet before message 9 so a late `final_offer` can be taken at once.

## 6. Estimating the floor

**Research.** Bayesian learning of the reservation price (Zeng and Sycara 1998), regression on the
opponent's concession curve (Hou 2004), Gaussian-process prediction of its next offers (IAMhaggler,
Williams et al. 2011). With three counters p1, p2, p3 and geometric decay, Aitken's formula gives
the limit: `R = p3 - (p3 - p2)^2 / ((p3 - p2) - (p2 - p1))`. Known failure: when step ratios rise
(slower than geometric) it underestimates the floor and pushes too hard. Every observed counter is
a hard upper bound on the floor.

**For us.** Useful as a secondary signal, not a stop rule: the bot stops on patience before its
floor, so a floor estimate mostly tells us whether a relationship charge is near (stabilise,
secure supply) and whether a large first concession means room (already `DEEP` in the policy).
The relationship charge in a finished practice result gives the supplier's true margin and cost
(`learnings.md`), which beats any curve fit for practice cases.

## 7. Procurement levers by supplier situation

**Research** (practice literature: Kraljic 1983, consultancy and CIPS sources; conventions, not
studies): classify the position first (leverage: compete and push price; bottleneck and strategic:
secure supply and joint value); answer a price-increase letter with a line-item breakdown weighted
by each driver's cost share; accept justified increases only index-linked or temporary; price
payment terms at both sides' cost of money; index clauses with a deadband of 3 to 5 %, a lag,
a cap, both directions and only the exposed cost share; threaten a second source only if it is
real; agree chargebacks before the dispute. Preferred-customer research (Schiele et al.): suppliers
reward attractive customers with capacity and price; forecast visibility and payment reliability
are what they ask for most. Collaborative but assertive buyers realise more value (Vantage
Partners survey, correlational).

**Playbook**, joined with our persona signals (`learnings.md`, Persona signals):

| Situation | Signal in the data | Give | Ask | Avoid |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cash short | "bank is watching", "pay earlier", cash discount | faster payment when its rate beats our 8 % (cash discounts imply 37 to 56 %/yr) | price | ignoring its ask when payment is fixed: say so and offer the next best currency |
| Fully booked | "fully booked", "allocates volumes" | its lead time, a firm 24-month volume, forecast | price at its standard speed | deep anchors (P10 patience 0.015), paying overtime for speed we do not value |
| Spare capacity | "second shift on hold" | volume, extra parts, long term | price | |
| Price frozen | "no room on price", "price list applies to all" | nothing on price | payment days, contract length, freight, start date | price pushes (no move, only lost patience) |
| Approval ladder | "above 2 % need the approval" | small steps (2 % or less), a reason the rep can forward to its boss | | one big ask that goes to a committee |
| Index-driven distributor | material share in its quote, clause offered | contract length only with a clause we can live with | deadband, share limited to material, falling series only | taking a 0 % deadband clause on a rising series (P02: score 0) |
| Price increase letter | letter above its drivers' index move | the index-weighted justified part, later start | notice period, start date, split | citing indices that rose (they confirm its case) |
| Stabilise, near cost | own-plant should-cost close to the quote | the price with the lowest C incl. relationship charge | terms | squeezing below sustainable margin (charge grows with the square) |
| Quality first | high scorecard ppm | | low ppm commitment, chargeback at least `cost_per_defect` | trading quality away for price unless C says so |

## 8. RFQs with two or three bidders

**Research.** Competition is worth more than negotiating skill: one extra bidder beats an optimally
negotiated deal (Bulow and Klemperer 1996). For complex, non-standard contracts, negotiation beats
a pure price auction because terms differ per bidder (Bajari, McMillan and Tadelis 2009). One
best-and-final round works; repeated ones teach bidders to hold back (practice sources).

**For us.** The current design matches: compare bids on total C, cite the cheapest rival's real
standing offer (a new argument every round), keep losing threads alive as the alternative.
Additions: one explicit best-and-final message per bidder near the end, not several; push the
bidder with the lowest C first and keep others warm with a question about capacity or delivery.
P05 is at 0.83, so RFQs are not where the points are.

## 9. Writing for LLM counterparts

**Research.** The largest AI negotiation competition (Vaccaro et al. 2025, about 120k to 180k
negotiations): warm agents beat cold ones on deal rate, joint value and counterpart satisfaction;
dominance claimed value but raised impasses; positivity, gratitude and questions predicted deals.
Buyers are harder for LLMs than sellers, and splitting a coded offer generator from an LLM narrator
lifted buyer deal rates from 27 % to 89 % (OG-Narrator, Xia et al. 2024): our architecture.
Asking about interests improves joint outcomes even when only one side does it (Thompson 1991).
Disappointment draws concessions, anger backfires on value disputes (Van Kleef). Objective
criteria and trades over positions (Fisher and Ury). LLMs drift toward a user who argues a side
(sycophancy rose from 50 to 79 % in one benchmark): a calm, reasoned position held over rounds
can move them, which is persuasion, not injection.

**Writing rules** for `buyer/writer.py` and the paragraph prompt in `buyer/llm.py`:

1. Open with one sentence that acknowledges its last message, specifically (what it moved, what it
   asked for).
2. Answer every request it made, even with no: "Payment terms are fixed in this agreement; what
   we can offer instead is ..." (P11).
3. One or two reasons per message, each a checkable fact next to its ID; more reasons dilute.
4. Frame every move as a trade: "If you can do X, we can do Y."
5. Ask one open question about its constraints ("What would make a price near X work for your
   planning?"). No "why" questions.
6. Express disappointment at the gap, never anger at the person.
7. Give the rep a forwardable rationale for its boss: figure, source, what we give in return.
8. Name our last step as last, once, and mean it.
9. No urgency, budget, target or missing alternative; no threats; no fake rivals; nothing aimed at
   the bot's instructions.

## 10. Experiment plan

The sandbox (D01, D02) is free and deterministic, so one run per variant measures the change.
Practice quota only for changes that won there; one change per batch.

| Order | Experiment | Where | Read out |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `FRACTION` 0.3 / 0.5 / 0.7 | D01, D02 | final price, rounds to `final_offer`, Σ gap |
| 2 | Round 1 with three equal-C sheets against one | D01, D02, then P07, P08, P18 | first counter, which sheet it picked |
| 3 | Hold back one currency (contract length or forecast) for round 2 or 3 | D01, then P07, P10 | its step after a currency move against a price move |
| 4 | Explicit answer to its stated need | P11 | price after round 2; back office tone |
| 5 | ppm headroom as currency | P11 | price per ppm point given against our 7 EUR |
| 6 | `BUYER_PUSH_FINAL` | cases with an alternative only | walks against gain |

Record each result in `learnings.md` (tag `arena`), including the ones that fail.

# Generalisation to the Live Final

How well the agent on `steffen/price-engine` (commit `9182604`) should carry over to Sunday: new
suppliers, up to a third of cases mixing supplier and case types practice never showed, some
citing the 08:00 release. Research on Saturday 10 October, evening: the kit's code, all 21 case
files, `logs/runs/`, `exports/`, the data package, and our agent on `arena-sim`. No practice
quota spent. Same conventions as `learnings.md`: date, tag, finding, evidence, consequence.

## Verdict

The code runs on every case structure we know. Its tuning is in-sample and unmeasured beyond
the ten hosted cases. The biggest gaps for Sunday: new suppliers get a neutral profile because
the release's letters and news never reach the persona code; one exception loses a whole case
(or every later wave); four or more bidders time out.

| # | Risk | Damage | Fix | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | an exception in a move or the wave poll | a case at its alternative (0 in 6 of 21), or all later waves | catch per move, keep polling | small |
| 2 | release rows invisible to SQL; most suppliers without text | neutral profile for new suppliers | read release rows via the ID index; scan the supplier's e-mails | small to medium |
| 3 | 4 or more bidders | timeouts, lost patience, ended threads | stop sending to the worst bidders after round 1 | medium, a tactics decision |
| 4 | missed phrasings in `SIGNALS` | traits not detected | widen to word stems | small |
| 5 | `price_unit` ignored | wrong-direction rival or order-price claims | divide by `price_unit` | small |

## Findings

### Robustness

- 2026-10-10 `rules` **Every known case structure runs end to end.** All 21 public case files,
  including the nine never hosted (P06, P09, P12 to P17, P19), played through `arena-sim`
  in-process with our agent and the package, no model: no exception, 0 to 1 s per case. Covers
  bundles (P07 4 parts, P15 3), the 3-bidder RFQ, `tooling_eur` (P06) and up to 75 term
  combinations (P09). The sim's supplier is a fixed script, so this checks code paths, not
  tactics. → Worth a test in `tests/` that plays every case file from `GET /v1/cases` this way
  (load them into `Sim(cases, pkg.facts)`, strip the `hosted` key).
- 2026-10-10 `rules` **One exception loses a case.** `play_case` has no guard around
  `Negotiator.setup` or `move`. Fields a hidden case may lack crash it: a rival quote without
  `unit_price` (`claims.py` `rival_quote`), an index clause without `material_share`
  (`writer.py` `FIELDS`), a scorecard without `quarter` (`claims.py` `scorecard`), a month not in
  `YYYY-MM` (`months_back`). The session then sits until the wave cap, which scores the
  alternative (0 in D01, P05, P06, P10, P14, P17). → Catch per move; on error send our last
  sheet again with the template e-mail.
- 2026-10-10 `rules` **One error stops the final.** `runner.play_waves` re-raises any non-403
  `ArenaError` from the case-list poll, and a network error after the client's retries is not
  caught at all (`arena_kit/client.py` `_call`). Every later wave is then lost; no human may
  restart. → Catch everything in the poll loop, log, sleep, poll again; a crashed case resumes
  with `GET /v1/sessions/{sid}` (a second `POST` is a 409 naming the session).

### Timing

- 2026-10-10 `rules` **Four bidders or more time out.** The arena answers one call per session at
  a time (`arena_kit/client.py`: "a call may wait for another call on the same session first").
  Supplier replies took 19 s median, 28 s p90 (121 moves in `logs/runs/`); our writer 1.8 s
  median, 6.3 s max (73 calls, none failed, 7 dropped by the filter). A thread waits about
  (N - 1) x 21 s for its next message against a 60 s limit:

  | Bidders | Wait at median | Wait at p90 | Rounds per thread in 390 s |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 2 | 23 s | 34 s | 9 / 6 |
  | 3 | 44 s | 66 s, late | 6 / 4 |
  | 4 | 65 s, late | late | 5 / 3 |

  P05 (3 bidders) had one late move in v5. No case file has more than 3 bidders, but hidden
  cases bring "new settings". → With 4 or more bidders, stop sending to the clearly worst ones
  after round 1; the writer's 20 s timeout matters little next to the supplier's reply time.

### Data and the Sunday release

- 2026-10-10 `rules` **The release reaches only part of the agent.** `DataPackage` finds
  `data/release-sunday/` next to the package, merges its `facts.json` (new IDs only) and puts its
  `data/*.csv` rows into the ID index for `lookup` and `ids`, never into SQLite
  (`arena_kit/data.py`, `_ids`). `personas.profile()`, `Negotiator.full_cost()` and the claims
  built from SQL (`po_lines`, `cost_drivers`, `documents`, `suppliers`) never see release rows,
  and document files resolve against the package root, not the release. Release IDs can still be
  cited. `design.md` says the release is "read at runtime"; that holds for `facts.json` only.
  → Read release rows through `pkg.ids(prefix)` / `pkg.lookup` (each row carries `root`) in
  `profile()` and the document claims. Check the CSV schema at 08:00.
- 2026-10-10 `data` **Most suppliers have no text.** Of 447 suppliers, 46 have documents, 31 news,
  18 quote remarks; the other 401 get the neutral profile (rate 7 %, no signals). A new supplier
  in the final is one of them or unknown to the package. → Its own e-mails and the release are
  the only persona source.
- 2026-10-10 `data` 15 of 108 quotes are priced per 100 (13) or per 1000 (2) pieces
  (`quotes.price_unit`). Rival-quote and order-history claims compare `unit_price` with the
  supplier's per-piece price without converting. → Divide by `price_unit` before comparing.
- 2026-10-10 `rules` **Structures only in unplayed cases** (case files): `tooling_eur` negotiable
  and lead time at most 84 days (P06), chargeback in the alternative (P12), index series PPI-C241
  in a clause (P16), fixed payment in a quality case (P12), a 3-part bundle (P15). Every case type
  and category goal appears in at least one hosted case. Only `incoterm` (D02) lies outside the
  fields the planner knows.

### Persona signals

- 2026-10-10 `data` **The patterns are not fitted to the practice suppliers**: the package's text
  is generated and its phrases recur, so all 10 suppliers of the unplayed cases get at least one
  trait. They miss other forms of the same phrases: "restructuring programme with its banks"
  (sup:70150), "negotiating with its banks" (sup:70280), "lowered its rating" (sup:70310),
  "bought their nickel and alloys forward" (sup:70730), "advertising free machine capacity"
  (sup:70250), "allocated in line with last year's call-offs" (sup:70410). "I cannot sign
  anything that lowers our margin now" (5 call notes) is a trait with no pattern. → Widen to word
  stems before the release adds new wording.
- 2026-10-10 `arena` **Supplier e-mails carry traits too:** 13 of 220 supplier e-mails in
  `exports/messages.jsonl` match `SIGNALS` (price_frozen sup:70530; spare_capacity sup:70210,
  70250, DEMO-J1; capacity_full sup:70240; cash_need sup:70210), including a sandbox supplier the
  package does not know. → Scanning each reply gives unknown suppliers a profile (untested in
  play).

### Tuning

- 2026-10-10 `arena` **Out-of-sample performance is unmeasured.** The 0.727 mean is in-sample:
  every constant was tuned on the same ten hosted cases and the other nine cannot be played.
  Runs of one case spread widely across v1 to v6 (P18 0.25 to 0.49 over seven runs, P08 0.40 to
  0.55), and with a model-written paragraph the wording changes per run while wording moves the
  price (`learnings.md`, takeaway 3). → Treat single-run moves below about 0.1 as noise.
- 2026-10-10 `rules` **Evidence behind each constant** in `buyer/policy.py` (from `git log -p`):

  | `ANCHOR` leverage 0.78 | P05, P08 / P18 (one template) | medium |

# Negotiation strategies: research for our buyer agent

Research report, 10 October 2026. Two inputs: (1) the literature on automated negotiation,
bargaining, procurement practice and LLM negotiators, gathered by ten parallel research agents;
(2) our own 62 logged practice sessions (`logs/sessions/`), read again to see which of those ideas
fit the arena's supplier bots. Each recommendation says what supports it and how to test it. Most
literature points were read from abstracts and summaries, not full papers: treat effect sizes as
directional (sources and confidence at the end).

## Summary

The current price engine scores a mean of **0.73** over the ten hosted cases (best run per case).
The gaps that remain are concentrated: P10 (0.68, 194k EUR from C_best), P08 (0.55, 79k), P18
(0.49, 37k), P11 (0.71, 28k), P07 (0.75, 23k), P02 (0.51, 23k).

What the traces show about the bots, in literature terms: a **behaviour-dependent conceder**
(Faratin, Sierra and Jennings' tactic family) that answers each of our steps with a smaller step
of its own, becomes a little more generous late, and ends the dance with `final_offer` once its
patience is used up. It ends the dance after 2 to 6 of our messages, so the 10-message limit
never binds. **The first counter decides most of the deal.**

Recommendations, ranked by expected gain against cost to build:

| # | Change | Why | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Make round 1 count:** three equal-C sheets (MESO), the strongest claims, a precise anchor with a reason | the first counter holds 40 to 100 % of our final price cut; MESOs anchor harder and reveal priorities | sandbox D01/D02, then P07, P08, P18 |

2. **It answers our steps at ρ < 1.** If we close the gap fully, the deal lands at

3. **ρ grows late** (D01: 0.2 early, 1 to 2 in the last rounds), the time-dependent part of the
   tactic. `final_offer` cuts this off before we reach it.
4. **`final_offer` arrives early:** after 2 to 6 of our messages, at a cu…952 tokens truncated…ponent model and a lenient

from the mean and spread of its offers). Shrinking concessions make the counterpart expect a limit
and counter less ambitiously (Tey, Schaerer, Madan and Swaab 2021, seven studies). Deadline
research: agreements cluster at the deadline (Roth, Murnighan and Schoumaker 1988), but here the
supplier's own patience is the effective deadline. Procurement practice: never give a concession
without asking for something specific in return.

- **Concede in currencies the supplier values and we do not.** The bot gives nothing without a

- **Shrink our steps visibly** (Tey et al.): the supplier reads them as our limit. Our steps
  already shrink; keep it, and say in words which step is the last.
- **Never move on a round where it did not move**, except with a currency (holding is free; an

## 5. Acceptance and the end of a thread

**Research.** The standard rule is AC_next: accept when its offer is at least as good as what we
would send next (most common in ANAC, Baarslag et al.); winners add a time rule that relaxes near
the deadline. Bargaining theory gives the expected-value form: accept now when
`C_now <= (1 - p) * E[C_next] + p * C_alt`, with p the chance the next push ends the thread.

**For us.**
- AC_next is in place (`theirs <= ours[-1]` accepts). Keep it.
- After `final_offer`, p is high (one walk in our pushes so far) and the expected gain of one more
  step is small (0 to 1 % in our traces). Accept unless `BUYER_PUSH_FINAL` data shows a net gain
  across several cases; in cases without an alternative (D01, P05, P06, P10, P14, P17) never push.
- Prepare the worst acceptable sheet before message 9 so a late `final_offer` can be taken at once.

## 6. Estimating the floor

**Research.** Bayesian learning of the reservation price (Zeng and Sycara 1998), regression on the
opponent's concession curve (Hou 2004), Gaussian-process prediction of its next offers (IAMhaggler,
Williams et al. 2011). With three counters p1, p2, p3 and geometric decay, Aitken's formula gives
the limit: `R = p3 - (p3 - p2)^2 / ((p3 - p2) - (p2 - p1))`. Known failure: when step ratios rise
(slower than geometric) it underestimates the floor and pushes too hard. Every observed counter is
a hard upper bound on the floor.

**For us.** Useful as a secondary signal, not a stop rule: the bot stops on patience before its
floor, so a floor estimate mostly tells us whether a relationship charge is near (stabilise,
secure supply) and whether a large first concession means room (already `DEEP` in the policy).
The relationship charge in a finished practice result gives the supplier's true margin and cost
(`learnings.md`), which beats any curve fit for practice cases.

## 7. Procurement levers by supplier situation

**Research** (practice literature: Kraljic 1983, consultancy and CIPS sources; conventions, not
studies): classify the position first (leverage: compete and push price; bottleneck and strategic:
secure supply and joint value); answer a price-increase letter with a line-item breakdown weighted
by each driver's cost share; accept justified increases only index-linked or temporary; price
payment terms at both sides' cost of money; index clauses with a deadband of 3 to 5 %, a lag,
a cap, both directions and only the exposed cost share; threaten a second source only if it is
real; agree chargebacks before the dispute. Preferred-customer research (Schiele et al.): suppliers
reward attractive customers with capacity and price; forecast visibility and payment reliability
are what they ask for most. Collaborative but assertive buyers realise more value (Vantage
Partners survey, correlational).

**Playbook**, joined with our persona signals (`learnings.md`, Persona signals):

| Situation | Signal in the data | Give | Ask | Avoid |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cash short | "bank is watching", "pay earlier", cash discount | faster payment when its rate beats our 8 % (cash discounts imply 37 to 56 %/yr) | price | ignoring its ask when payment is fixed: say so and offer the next best currency |
| Fully booked | "fully booked", "allocates volumes" | its lead time, a firm 24-month volume, forecast | price at its standard speed | deep anchors (P10 patience 0.015), paying overtime for speed we do not value |
| Spare capacity | "second shift on hold" | volume, extra parts, long term | price | |
| Price frozen | "no room on price", "price list applies to all" | nothing on price | payment days, contract length, freight, start date | price pushes (no move, only lost patience) |
| Approval ladder | "above 2 % need the approval" | small steps (2 % or less), a reason the rep can forward to its boss | | one big ask that goes to a committee |
| Index-driven distributor | material share in its quote, clause offered | contract length only with a clause we can live with | deadband, share limited to material, falling series only | taking a 0 % deadband clause on a rising series (P02: score 0) |
| Price increase letter | letter above its drivers' index move | the index-weighted justified part, later start | notice period, start date, split | citing indices that rose (they confirm its case) |
| Stabilise, near cost | own-plant should-cost close to the quote | the price with the lowest C incl. relationship charge | terms | squeezing below sustainable margin (charge grows with the square) |
| Quality first | high scorecard ppm | | low ppm commitment, chargeback at least `cost_per_defect` | trading quality away for price unless C says so |

## 8. RFQs with two or three bidders

**Research.** Competition is worth more than negotiating skill: one extra bidder beats an optimally
negotiated deal (Bulow and Klemperer 1996). For complex, non-standard contracts, negotiation beats
a pure price auction because terms differ per bidder (Bajari, McMillan and Tadelis 2009). One
best-and-final round works; repeated ones teach bidders to hold back (practice sources).

**For us.** The current design matches: compare bids on total C, cite the cheapest rival's real
standing offer (a new argument every round), keep losing threads alive as the alternative.
Additions: one explicit best-and-final message per bidder near the end, not several; push the
bidder with the lowest C first and keep others warm with a question about capacity or delivery.
P05 is at 0.83, so RFQs are not where the points are.

## 9. Writing for LLM counterparts

**Research.** The largest AI negotiation competition (Vaccaro et al. 2025, about 120k to 180k
negotiations): warm agents beat cold ones on deal rate, joint value and counterpart satisfaction;
dominance claimed value but raised impasses; positivity, gratitude and questions predicted deals.
Buyers are harder for LLMs than sellers, and splitting a coded offer generator from an LLM narrator
lifted buyer deal rates from 27 % to 89 % (OG-Narrator, Xia et al. 2024): our architecture.
Asking about interests improves joint outcomes even when only one side does it (Thompson 1991).
Disappointment draws concessions, anger backfires on value disputes (Van Kleef). Objective
criteria and trades over positions (Fisher and Ury). LLMs drift toward a user who argues a side
(sycophancy rose from 50 to 79 % in one benchmark): a calm, reasoned position held over rounds
can move them, which is persuasion, not injection.

**Writing rules** for `buyer/writer.py` and the paragraph prompt in `buyer/llm.py`:

1. Open with one sentence that acknowledges its last message, specifically (what it moved, what it
   asked for).
2. Answer every request it made, even with no: "Payment terms are fixed in this agreement; what
   we can offer instead is ..." (P11).
3. One or two reasons per message, each a checkable fact next to its ID; more reasons dilute.
4. Frame every move as a trade: "If you can do X, we can do Y."
5. Ask one open question about its constraints ("What would make a price near X work for your
   planning?"). No "why" questions.
6. Express disappointment at the gap, never anger at the person.
7. Give the rep a forwardable rationale for its boss: figure, source, what we give in return.
8. Name our last step as last, once, and mean it.
9. No urgency, budget, target or missing alternative; no threats; no fake rivals; nothing aimed at
   the bot's instructions.

## 10. Experiment plan

The sandbox (D01, D02) is free and deterministic, so one run per variant measures the change.
Practice quota only for changes that won there; one change per batch.

| Order | Experiment | Where | Read out |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `FRACTION` 0.3 / 0.5 / 0.7 | D01, D02 | final price, rounds to `final_offer`, Σ gap |
| 2 | Round 1 with three equal-C sheets against one | D01, D02, then P07, P08, P18 | first counter, which sheet it picked |
| 3 | Hold back one currency (contract length or forecast) for round 2 or 3 | D01, then P07, P10 | its step after a currency move against a price move |

| 5 | ppm headroom as currency | P11 | price per ppm point given against our 7 EUR |
| 6 | `BUYER_PUSH_FINAL` | cases with an alternative only | walks against gain |

Record each result in `learnings.md` (tag `arena`), including the ones that fail.

import copy
import secrets
import socket
import threading
import time

import pytest
import uvicorn
from arena_kit import ArenaClient, RemoteTable, complete_offer
from arena_kit.sim import Sim, create_app, load_cases

from buyer import economics, runner
from buyer.policy import Negotiator
from buyer.runner import play_case


@pytest.fixture
def sim_url():
    """arena-sim on a free local port, with a clock that never moves (no 60-second timeouts)."""
    server_state = Sim(load_cases(), clock=lambda: 1_000_000.0)
    with socket.socket() as s:
        s.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
        port = s.getsockname()[1]
    server = uvicorn.Server(uvicorn.Config(create_app(server_state), port=port, log_level="warning"))
    thread = threading.Thread(target=server.run, daemon=True)
    thread.start()
    while not server.started:
        time.sleep(0.01)
    yield f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}"
    server.should_exit = True
    thread.join()


def test_buyer_closes_a_deal(sim_url, tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    key = ArenaClient(sim_url).register(f"test-{secrets.token_hex(3)}", "sim")["api_key"]
    client = ArenaClient(sim_url, key, rate=1000)
    monkeypatch.setattr(runner, "RUNS", tmp_path)
    result = play_case(RemoteTable(client), "case:S01")
    assert result["deal"]
    assert 0 <= result["score"] <= 1


def test_terms_cover_the_need_when_the_price_is_low():
    """A 12-month contract leaves half a 2-year need to the fallback: at a low price we cover it."""
    case = copy.deepcopy(load_cases()["case:S01"])
    case["buyer"]["horizon_years"] = 2
    case["negotiable"].append("contract_months")
    case["fixed_terms"].pop("contract_months")
    case["term_options"]["contract_months"] = [12, 24]
    est = economics.estimate(case, {}, 0.07)
    quote = complete_offer(case, {"unit_price": case["buyer"]["current_unit_price"], "contract_months": 12})
    terms, c = economics.plan_terms(case, {}, est, quote, quote["unit_price"] * 0.8)
    assert terms["contract_months"] == 24
    assert c < economics.cost(case, {**quote, "unit_price": terms["unit_price"]}, {}, est)


def reply(status, terms, offer="offer:S-1"):
    return [{"from": "supplier", "status": status, "term_sheets": [{"term_sheet_id": offer, "terms": terms}]}]


def test_close_never_beats_the_alternative():
    """A standing sheet dearer than the alternative is never accepted."""
    case = copy.deepcopy(load_cases()["case:S01"])
    case["buyer"]["alternative"] = {"kind": "quote", "ref": "quote:alt", "terms": {"unit_price": 10.0}}
    dear = {"unit_price": 15.88, "payment_days": 30}
    threads = {"sup:S": reply("final_offer", dear)}
    neg = Negotiator(case)
    neg.setup("sup:S", threads["sup:S"])
    assert economics.cost(case, dear, {}) > economics.c_alt(case)
    assert neg.close(threads)["message"]["action"]["type"] == "walk_away"


def test_adopts_its_index_clause_only_when_its_sheet_costs_less():
    """A supplier's index clause on a rising series is taken only when its sheet, clause included,
    costs less than its last one; never when it breaks a must-have."""
    case = copy.deepcopy(load_cases()["case:S01"])
    clause = {"series": "WB-CU", "material_share": 0.2, "deadband_pct": 0, "base_month": "2026-08"}
    case["negotiable"].append("index_clause")
    case["fixed_terms"].pop("index_clause")
    case["term_options"]["index_clause"] = [None, clause]
    case["buyer"]["index_paths"] = {"WB-CU": 0.05}
    quote = {"unit_price": 15.88, "payment_days": 30, "index_clause": None}

    def side(case):
        neg = Negotiator(case)
        s = neg.setup("sup:S", reply("open", quote))
        assert s.terms["index_clause"] is None
        s.ours.append(s.anchor)
        return neg, s

    neg, s = side(case)
    neg.adopt(s, [{"term_sheet_id": "offer:S-2", "terms": {**quote, "unit_price": 15.80, "index_clause": clause}}])
    assert s.terms["index_clause"] is None  # a token price cut does not pay for the clause
    neg.adopt(s, [{"term_sheet_id": "offer:S-3", "terms": {**quote, "unit_price": 14.0, "index_clause": clause}}])
    assert s.terms["index_clause"] == clause  # a real cut does

    case["buyer"]["must_haves"] = [{"field": "index_clause", "op": "==", "value": None}]

"""Offline regressions for PR12 911b35b; uses no credentials or hosted API."""
from types import SimpleNamespace

from buyer.claims import ClaimBank
from buyer.policy import Negotiator


def lost_attachment():
    sid = "sup:NEW"
    side = SimpleNamespace(
        asks=["proof"], attached=set(), pending={"keys": [], "state": "open"},
        state="open", late=0,
    )
    neg = Negotiator.__new__(Negotiator)
    neg.case = {"parts": ["part:NEW"]}
    neg.bank = SimpleNamespace(
        ids=lambda prefix: ["fc:NEW@2026-09"],
        fact=lambda ref: {"volume_per_year": 100, "change_pct": 10.0},
    )
    neg.sides = {sid: side}
    neg.note = lambda *args, **kwargs: None
    assert len(neg.attachments(side)) == 1
    neg.rollback(sid)  # the supplier never received the message
    assert neg.attachments(side) == []
    print("CONFIRMED: rejected forecast attachment is never retried")


def invented_notice():
    pkg = SimpleNamespace(lookup=lambda ref: None)
    case = {
        "refs": ["doc:unseen-letter", "ctr:unseen-contract"],
        "trigger_doc": "doc:unseen-letter", "type": "price_increase",
        "parts": [], "buyer": {},
    }
    bank = ClaimBank(pkg, case)
    assert bank.notice("sup:NEW") is None
    claims = bank.demo_refs()
    assert len(claims) == 1 and "less notice" in claims[0]["text"]
    print("CONFIRMED: missing documents fabricate inadequate notice allegation")


lost_attachment()
invented_notice()

Full scoped review completed at `911b35b037e4574025343fe9803236c9a983932b`. Shared checkout unchanged.

**Two confirmed P2 findings:**

1. **Commit attachment delivery only after a successful send**  
   `buyer/policy.py:435–445`: `attachments()` immediately adds `"forecast"` to `s.attached`. A subsequent 409 invokes `rollback()`, which restores offers/claims but not attachment state. Further supplier requests receive no forecast although the supplier never received the original message. Move attachment bookkeeping into `commit()` or undo it on rollback.

2. **Do not invent a notice violation when documents are unavailable**  
   `buyer/claims.py:264–268`: `demo_refs()` emits “Your letter … gives less notice than our agreement provides for” when the letter fact is missing. `foreign` covers any unknown case references, including new suppliers, not just D01. This promotes absent evidence into a high-strength factual accusation. Omit the notice argument until both documents establish the comparison.

Both reproduced offline by:

```sh
PYTHONPATH=/private/tmp/codacabana-pr12-full-review \
/private/tmp/codacabana-buyer-fixes/.venv/bin/python \
/private/tmp/codacabana-claims-review/repro.py
```

**Limitations worth tracking, not additional merge blockers:**

- `claims.py:200–204` still reads document claims through base SQLite and `pkg.root`; Sunday release documents do not produce these cited claims.
- Persona text scanning now correctly uses package IDs and `document()`, including release documents with a full base SQLite package. A facts-only package still returns a neutral profile before scanning (`personas.py:66–70`).
- Regex reader does not represent denial/contradiction or conditional preferences. That is an architectural limitation, not proof of an observed bug.
- Existing blanket documentation claim that distributors reject every deadband remains false (`docs/learnings.md:43`). Earlier replay analysis supplies exact counterexamples.
- `docs/negotiation-research.md` labels 0.73 as best-per-case, appropriately. Its recommendation that one sandbox run measures policy improvement is too strong given its own acknowledgment that wording can change outcomes; do not treat that as deployment evidence.

No hosted calls, credentials, external messages, or code changes.

+"""Read every committed practice/sandbox replay without accessing hosted services."""
+import hashlib
+import json
+import re
+from collections import Counter, defaultdict
+from pathlib import Path
+from statistics import mean
+
+from arena_kit import total_cost
+from arena_kit.cost import cost_breakdown
+
+ROOT = Path('/private/tmp/codacabana-pr12-full-review')
+OUT = Path('/private/tmp/pr12-log-review/report.json')
+
+
+def summary(rows):
+    return {
+        'attempts': len(rows), 'deals': sum(r['deal'] for r in rows),
+        'mean': mean(r['score'] for r in rows),
+        'minimum': min(r['score'] for r in rows), 'maximum': max(r['score'] for r in rows),
+        'no_deals': sum(not r['deal'] for r in rows),
+        'end_reasons': dict(Counter(r['end_reason'] for r in rows)),
+        'timeout_events': sum(len(r['timeouts']) for r in rows),
+        'sessions_with_timeouts': sum(bool(r['timeouts']) for r in rows),
+    }
+
+
+cases = {}
+for path in (ROOT/'logs/cases').glob('*.json'):
+    cases.update({c['case_id']: c for c in json.loads(path.read_text())})
+rows = []
+for path in sorted((ROOT/'logs/sessions').glob('*/*.json')):
+    s = json.loads(path.read_text())
+    if s['set'] not in ('practice', 'sandbox'):
+        continue
+    r = s['result']
+    assert r['ended']
+    c = cases[s['case_id']]
+    run = ROOT/'logs/runs'/path.name
+    notes = json.loads(run.read_text()).get('notes', []) if run.exists() else []
+    row = {
+        'session_id': s['session_id'], 'case_id': s['case_id'], 'environment': s['set'],
+        'source': str(path.relative_to(ROOT)), 'sha256': hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
+        'score': r['score'], 'deal': r['deal'], 'end_reason': s['end_reason'],

"""Read every committed practice/sandbox replay without accessing hosted services."""
import hashlib
import json
import re
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from pathlib import Path
from statistics import mean

from arena_kit import total_cost
from arena_kit.cost import cost_breakdown

ROOT = Path('/private/tmp/codacabana-pr12-full-review')
OUT = Path('/private/tmp/pr12-log-review/report.json')


def summary(rows):
    return {
        'attempts': len(rows), 'deals': sum(r['deal'] for r in rows),
        'mean': mean(r['score'] for r in rows),
        'minimum': min(r['score'] for r in rows), 'maximum': max(r['score'] for r in rows),
        'no_deals': sum(not r['deal'] for r in rows),
        'end_reasons': dict(Counter(r['end_reason'] for r in rows)),
        'timeout_events': sum(len(r['timeouts']) for r in rows),
        'sessions_with_timeouts': sum(bool(r['timeouts']) for r in rows),
    }


cases = {}
for path in (ROOT/'logs/cases').glob('*.json'):
    cases.update({c['case_id']: c for c in json.loads(path.read_text())})
rows = []
for path in sorted((ROOT/'logs/sessions').glob('*/*.json')):
    s = json.loads(path.read_text())
    if s['set'] not in ('practice', 'sandbox'):
        continue
    r = s['result']
    assert r['ended']
    c = cases[s['case_id']]
    run = ROOT/'logs/runs'/path.name
    notes = json.loads(run.read_text()).get('notes', []) if run.exists() else []
    row = {
        'session_id': s['session_id'], 'case_id': s['case_id'], 'environment': s['set'],
        'source': str(path.relative_to(ROOT)), 'sha256': hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
        'score': r['score'], 'deal': r['deal'], 'end_reason': s['end_reason'],
        'terms': r.get('terms'), 'supplier_id': r.get('supplier_id'),
        'costs': {k: r.get(k) for k in ('c_open', 'c_deal', 'c_alt', 'c_best')},
        'breakdown': r.get('cost_breakdown'), 'must_haves_ok': r.get('must_haves_ok'),
        'gap_eur': round(r['c_deal']-r['c_best'],2) if r.get('c_deal') is not None else None,
        'first_note_time': min((n['t'] for n in notes), default=None),
        'runtime_commit': None, 'timeouts': [], 'threads': {},
    }
    if row['deal']:
        calc = cost_breakdown(c, r['terms'])
        errors = {k: round(v-r['cost_breakdown'][k],8) for k,v in calc.items() if k!='relationship'}
        row['public_cost_component_errors'] = errors
        assert max(abs(v) for v in errors.values()) < .011
        assert abs(sum(r['cost_breakdown'].values()) - r['c_deal']) < .011
        if not c['buyer'].get('relationship_eur_per_point'):
            terms = r['terms']
            cost0 = total_cost(c, {**terms, 'unit_price':0})
            slope = total_cost(c, {**terms, 'unit_price':1}) - cost0
            price = (r['c_best']-cost0)/slope
            row['price_to_match_benchmark_at_final_other_terms'] = round(price,6)
            row['price_reduction_pct_to_match'] = round((1-price/terms['unit_price'])*100,4)
            row['benchmark_price_limitation'] = 'Arithmetic only; not demonstrated feasible or acceptable.'
    for i,event in enumerate(r['trace']):
        m = event['move']
        if m.get('type')=='timeout':
            row['timeouts'].append(i)
        sid = m.get('supplier_id') if event['actor']=='buyer' else event['actor']
        if not sid:
            # Single supplier buyer traces sometimes omit the supplier field.
            sid = next(iter(s['opening'])) if len(s.get('opening',{}))==1 else None
        if sid is None:
            continue
        thread = row['threads'].setdefault(sid, {'supplier_offers':[], 'buyer_proposals':[], 'claims':[]})
        if event['actor']=='buyer':
            for sheet in m.get('term_sheets',[]):
                thread['buyer_proposals'].append({'trace_index':i,'round':event['round'],'terms':sheet['terms']})
        else:
            thread['supplier_offers'].append({
                'trace_index':i,'round':event['round'],'status':m.get('status'),
                'terms':m.get('terms'), 'alternatives':m.get('alternatives',[]),
                'reasons':event.get('reasons',[]),
            })
            for claim in m.get('claim_results',[]):
                thread['claims'].append({'trace_index':i,**claim})
    for sid,thread in row['threads'].items():
        offers = [o for o in thread['supplier_offers'] if (o.get('terms') or {}).get('unit_price')]
        bids = thread['buyer_proposals']
        if not offers:
            continue
        opening = offers[0]['terms']['unit_price']
        if bids:
            thread['opening_anchor_below_quote_pct'] = round((1-bids[0]['terms']['unit_price']/opening)*100,4)
        first_counter = next((o for o in offers if o['round']>0),None)
        last = offers[-1]['terms']['unit_price']
        if first_counter:
            counter = first_counter['terms']['unit_price']
            thread['first_counter_price'] = counter
            thread['later_price_improvement'] = round(counter-last,6)
            thread['first_counter_fraction_of_total_price_move'] = round((opening-counter)/(opening-last),5) if opening!=last else None
        thread['price_path'] = [o['terms']['unit_price'] for o in offers]
        thread['price_path_warning'] = 'Price movement is not comparable total-cost movement when terms change.'
    rows.append(row)

assert len({r['session_id'] for r in rows})==len(rows)
byid = {r['session_id']:r for r in rows}
batches = {}
for path in sorted((ROOT/'logs').glob('*.log')):
    ids = re.findall(r'^\S+ session ([0-9a-f]+)$',path.read_text(),re.MULTILINE)
    members = [byid[sid] for sid in ids if sid in byid]
    batches[path.name] = {
        'source':str(path.relative_to(ROOT)), 'session_ids':ids,
        'missing_exports':list(set(ids)-set(byid)),
        'summary':summary(members) if members else None,
        'case_results':{r['case_id']:{'session':r['session_id'],'score':r['score']} for r in members},
    }
groups=defaultdict(list)
for row in rows:
    groups[row['case_id']].append(row)
bycase={}
for cid,members in sorted(groups.items()):
    best=max(members,key=lambda r:r['score'])
    dated=[r for r in members if r['first_note_time'] is not None]
    latest=max(dated,key=lambda r:r['first_note_time']) if dated else None
    bycase[cid]={
        **summary(members), 'best_session':best['session_id'],'best_gap_eur':best['gap_eur'],
        'best_terms':best['terms'],'best_breakdown':best['breakdown'],
        'latest_with_run_timestamp':latest['session_id'] if latest else None,
        'latest_score':latest['score'] if latest else None,
        'undated_sessions':len(members)-len(dated),
        'best_price_to_match_benchmark':best.get('price_to_match_benchmark_at_final_other_terms'),
        'best_additional_price_cut_pct':best.get('price_reduction_pct_to_match'),
    }
export_ids={json.loads(line)['session_id'] for line in (ROOT/'exports/sessions.jsonl').read_text().splitlines()}
report={
    'snapshot_commit':'911b35b037e4574025343fe9803236c9a983932b',
    'scope':'All local complete practice/sandbox session exports and run batches at pinned commit.',
    'inventory':{'sessions':len(rows),'export_table_sessions':len(export_ids),
                 'export_table_sessions_absent_from_logs':sorted(export_ids-set(byid)),
                 'run_files':len(list((ROOT/'logs/runs').glob('*.json')))},
    'environments':{env:summary([r for r in rows if r['environment']==env]) for env in ['practice','sandbox']},
    'limitations':[
        'All attempts mixes historical policies and experiments; not current-policy expected score.',
        'No causal effect of aggression can be inferred from these uncontrolled comparisons.',
        'Undated exports prevent claiming a definitive latest result except explicit batch membership.',
        'Official cost breakdown is actual expenditure, not an attribution of gap to unknown optimal terms.',
        'No hidden optimal package or supplier economics is reconstructed.',
        'Benchmark-equivalent prices are arithmetic targets, not evidence of achievable deals.',
        'Sandbox and practice remain separate; exports tables duplicate session exports.',
    ],
    'by_case':bycase,'batches':batches,'sessions':rows,
}
OUT.write_text(json.dumps(report,indent=2,allow_nan=False)+'\n')
print(json.dumps({'inventory':report['inventory'],'environments':report['environments'],'by_case':bycase},indent=2))

Entreguei análise completa em `/private/tmp/pr12-log-review/`:

- `report.txt`: diagnóstico detalhado em inglês.
- `report.json`: 130 sessões, custos, trajetórias, alegações e proveniência.
- `report.csv`: tabela por sessão.
- `analyze.py`: reprodução offline.
- `summary.json`: resumo numérico por caso.

**Conclusão: agressividade insuficiente não explica tudo.** Há evidências concretas de perda por cobertura, custo de relacionamento, concessões desnecessárias, timeouts e argumentos inadequados.

**Achado mais acionável:** P05 `8c829c180671cc22`, trace 12: fornecedor concordou com **27,86 / 14 dias / entrega 35 dias**. Buyer trace 13 subiu para **28,07**, mesmos termos; fornecedor confirmou no trace 14. Resultado: **€1.782,03 piores**, sem contrapartida.

**Mais agressividade pode piorar:** D01 com demais termos idênticos:

- `39ecc97df8525399`: preço 48,90, score **0,997854**.
- `5a76c1f9a1ef4623`: preço 48,50, score **0,968747**.
- Economia em preço/pagamento €3.221,33; aumento da penalidade de relacionamento €4.391,03. Custo total **€1.169,70 maior**.

D01 `212404b7930bfc68`: insistir em 49,60 após oferta final 49,70 levou à retirada e score zero.

**Cobertura:** 65 practice + 65 sandbox, 130 sessões únicas; tabela exports com 32 sessões é subconjunto. Os componentes públicos dos **113 acordos** reproduzem os resultados oficiais até €0,01.

**Confiança:** practice tem 229 verificações aprovadas, 29 duplicadas, 9 irrelevantes e 2 contraditas; sandbox 107 aprovadas e 1 contradita. As contradições identificadas incluem `2,637` interpretado como `2.637` ppm e índice de ambiente errado.

O relatório diferencia melhores resultados de médias históricas, apresenta primeiro/último apenas entre registros datados, mantém os ambientes separados e não confunde propostas antigas com ofertas ainda disponíveis. Recomenda corrigir também as afirmações documentais “ceiling <0.9” e “recusam qualquer deadband”, que os dados não sustentam.

# AGENTS.md

Rules for AI coding agents in this repo. Humans follow them too.

Hackathon repo, EHL Grand Finale, Munich, 10 to 11 Oct 2026. Code freeze and Live Final Sunday
12:00. Working agent first, polish second.

## Rules

- Do not preserve backward compatibility. Remove obsolete paths instead of adding layers,
  fallbacks or migrations.
- Choose the simplest implementation that fully meets the current requirement. No speculative
  abstractions, configuration or indirection.
- Grow in layers on a product that already works. Never trade a working agent for unfinished
  complexity.
- Keep components modular and concerns separated.
- Read `arena_kit` (in `.venv`) before writing a helper: cost function, quote parsing, data lookup
  and runners exist. We wrap the kit, never patch it. Guide:
  https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit/tree/main/starter-kit
- Never commit secrets. Keys live in `.env`. Never print, log or paste the arena key anywhere.
- All changes go through a PR against `main`, reviewed by one teammate. Branch `<firstname>/<topic>`.
  Agents may commit, push their branch and `gh pr create`; never push to `main`, force-push or merge.
- Run `uv run pytest -q && uv run ruff check .` before every PR.
- No em-dashes in prose or copy. Be terse: after an action, state what changed in three lines.

## The challenge

We are the purchasing team of Hollerau Pumpenwerke. Our agent negotiates by e-mail with Tacto's
supplier bots (LLM personas with hidden economics) and closes one term sheet per case, or walks.

- **Score** per case: `(C_open - C_deal) / (C_open - C_best)`, clipped to 0..1. C is total cost
  over the horizon (price, uncovered need, payment, freight, lead time, quality, tooling, index
  clause, relationship charge), computed exactly by `arena_kit.total_cost`. No deal scores the
  alternative (0 if none). A broken must-have scores 0.
- **Live Final**: five waves of hidden cases, 8 minutes each, a wave's cases in parallel. Wave
  score = mean case score x 100; total = sum. New suppliers; up to a third mix supplier and case
  types practice never shows; some cite the Sunday 08:00 data release.

**Hard rules, breaking one can disqualify us:**
- No human in the loop during the final. The runner starts before 12:00 and is left alone.
- Agent code never calls `/v1/events`, `/v1/events/stream`, `/screen`, `/v1/screen`,
  `/leaderboard`, `/v1/leaderboard`, `/results`, `/v1/results`.
- One key per team. No attacks on the arena or other teams (prompt-injecting bots counts).
- The final runs the commit we submit at 12:00. No pushes after that.

**Hard limits:**
- 60 s per message per thread from the supplier's reply; three timeouts in a row end the thread.
- 10 messages per thread, up to 3 term sheets per message, every sheet carries every `negotiable`
  field.
- Max 3 claim checks per message, one per sentence, ID and figure in the same sentence. A wrong
  figure or unknown ID is `contradicted` and costs trust.
- 10 calls/s and 10 open sessions per key.
- **Practice quota: 200 sessions per rolling 24 h for the whole team.** Sandbox (`case:D01`,
  `case:D02`) and the local simulator are free.

## Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `docs/learnings.md` | **read first**: what we know about the arena, suppliers and data, with evidence |
| `docs/design.md` | the agent we are building: modules, data, policy, build order |
| `docs/challenge.md`, `api.md`, `submission.md` | Tacto's brief, API and cost formula, hand-in (upstream copies) |
| `buyer/policy.py`, `runner.py` | the price engine: per-thread policy and the loop that plays a case (`docs/design.md`, Implemented) |
| `buyer/economics.py`, `claims.py`, `personas.py`, `writer.py`, `llm.py` | C and term planning, claim bank, persona signals, e-mail and model paragraph |
| `buyer/cli.py` | `buyer play`, `buyer run`, `buyer pull` |
| `tests/` | end to end against `arena-sim`, no network, no model |
| `exports/` | Saturday probe sessions as CSV/JSONL; schema in `exports/README.md` |
| `analysis/explore.py` | data package exploration: profiles, persona signals, report page |
| `data/package/` | the data package (gitignored); Sunday also `data/release-sunday/` |
| `logs/sessions/<set>/` | finished sessions with trace and back office (gitignored; Saturday's committed with `-f`) |
| `logs/runs/`, `logs/practice-v*.log` | our decisions per move (anchor, terms, claims, prices) and the practice run logs |

The MCP server `arena-data` (`.mcp.json`) gives SQL, ID lookup and documents over the package.

## Commands

```sh
uv sync                                         # install (Python 3.12)
uv run arena data                               # data package into data/
uv run arena me                                 # key works? quota left?
uv run buyer play case:D01 -v                   # sandbox: free
uv run buyer play case:P01 -v                   # practice: costs 1 of the team's 200
uv run buyer run --set practice --parallel 10   # all hosted practice cases: costs 10
uv run buyer pull --set practice                # finished sessions -> logs/sessions/
uv run arena-sim serve --no-clock --data data/package   # local API, scripted supplier
uv run --with pandas python analysis/explore.py # data package -> analysis/out/
```

`--agent naive` plays the kit's baseline instead of ours.

## Working on the negotiation agent

- **Code owns numbers, the model owns words.** Every binding value (sheet, accept, walk away) is
  computed or checked in code with `total_cost` and `must_haves_ok`; every figure in an e-mail
  comes from code next to its data ID.
- **Never accept** a sheet that breaks a must-have or costs more than the alternative. Price
  unstated fields at the supplier's standard terms (`arena_kit.docs.standard_terms`).
- **Read the supplier.** What moves it is in the data (call notes, letters, news, quote remarks,
  payment history, scorecards). Trade what is cheap for us for what it values.
- **Score every lever per case.** The same term helps in one case and hurts in the next
  (coverage, payment days, start date, index clause, contract length).
- **Generalise.** No logic keyed on case or supplier IDs; runtime knowledge from the data package
  is fine if it works for unseen suppliers.
- **Don't leak** urgency, budget, a missing alternative or the target price.
- **Every model call has a hard timeout** well under 60 s, and the move still goes out if it
  fails. Measure latency per move.

## The learning loop

1. Try on the simulator or sandbox first. Spend practice quota only on a change you expect to
   help; check `uv run arena me` before batch runs.
2. After practice: `uv run buyer pull`, read `logs/sessions/` (trace, back office, cost breakdown).
3. Find why C_deal missed C_best, change the agent, score candidate sheets offline, play again.
4. Record each finding in `docs/learnings.md` in the same PR: date, tag (`arena` / `data` /
   `rules`), finding, evidence (session, case or data ID), consequence for the agent. Untested
   ideas go under Hypotheses; correct or delete entries that turn out wrong. Design changes go
   into `docs/design.md`. No new doc files without a reason.

## Sunday

- 08:00: `uv run arena data` again; the release lands in `data/release-sunday/`.
- 09:00: pre-flight, one practice case through the final machine and setup.
- 11:30: checklist in `docs/submission.md` (key, data, LLM credits, power, no sleep, log file).
- Before 12:00, from `main`: `uv run buyer run --set final --parallel 10 -v 2>&1 | tee logs/final.log`,
  then submit that commit hash on ehl.gg.

def money(x):
    return f"EUR {x:.2f}"


def per_unit(fact):
    """Pieces a recorded price covers: 15 of 108 quotes and some orders are priced per 100 or 1000."""
    try:
        return int(fact.get("price_unit") or 1) or 1
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return 1


class ClaimBank:
    """Arguments for one case. `pkg` is the data package (or None); the case's own `facts` win."""

    def __init__(self, pkg, case):
        self.pkg, self.case = pkg, case
        self.facts = case.get("facts") or {}
        self.refs = list(case.get("refs") or [])
        # a case whose refs the package does not know (the sandbox's demo world)
        self.foreign = bool(self.refs) and pkg is not None and not any(pkg.lookup(r) for r in self.refs)

    def fact(self, ref):
        if ref in self.facts:
            return self.facts[ref]
        return None if self.foreign or self.pkg is None else self.pkg.lookup(ref)

    def ids(self, prefix):
        out = set() if self.foreign or self.pkg is None else set(self.pkg.ids(prefix))
        out |= {k for k in self.facts if k.startswith(prefix)}
        out |= {r for r in self.refs if r.startswith(prefix)}
        return sorted(out)

    def query(self, sql, params=()):
        if self.foreign or self.pkg is None:
            return []
        try:
            return self.pkg.query(sql, params)
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - a package without SQLite: facts only
            return []

    # -- single arguments ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def should_cost(self, part, sid, quote):
        best = None
        for ref in self.ids("cost:"):
            f = self.fact(ref)
            if not f or f.get("part") != part or not f.get("unit_cost"):
                continue
            if ref.endswith("-" + sid.split(":")[-1]):
                best = (ref, f)
                break
            if best is None and "-" not in ref.split(":")[-1]:
                best = (ref, f)
        if not best:
            return None
        ref, f = best
        if quote and f["unit_cost"] >= quote * 0.98:
            return None  # above or near its price: argues its case
        return {
            "kind": "should_cost",
            "ids": [ref],
            "text": f"Our bottom-up should-cost estimate for this part is {money(f['unit_cost'])} per unit ({ref}).",
            "strength": 5,
        }

    def order_history(self, part, sid, quote):
        rows = self.query(
            "SELECT id FROM po_lines WHERE part_id = ? AND supplier_id = ? ORDER BY order_date DESC LIMIT 3",
            (part, sid),
        )
        facts = [(r["id"], self.fact(r["id"])) for r in rows]
        facts = [(i, f) for i, f in facts if f and f.get("unit_price")]
        if len(facts) < 2:
            return None
        prices = [f["unit_price"] for _, f in facts]
        unit = per_unit(facts[0][1])
        if quote and min(prices) / unit >= quote:
            return None  # the figure stays as recorded (per 100 or 1000 where priced so): that is what is checked
        ids = [i for i, _ in facts]
        each = f" per {unit} units" if unit != 1 else ""
        if len(set(prices)) == 1:
            text = f"Our last {len(ids)} orders for this part were at {money(prices[0])}{each} ({', '.join(ids)})."
        else:
            listed = " and ".join(money(p) for p in prices)
            text = f"Our last orders for this part were at {listed}{each} ({', '.join(ids)})."
        return {"kind": "order_history", "ids": ids, "text": text, "strength": 4}

    def notice(self, sid):
        doc = self.case.get("trigger_doc")
        f = self.fact(doc) if doc else None
        if not f or f.get("days") is None:
            return None
        ctr = next((r for r in self.refs if r.startswith("ctr:") and "#" not in r), None)
        c = self.fact(ctr) if ctr else None
        if not c or c.get("days") is None or f["days"] >= c["days"]:
            return None
        text = (
            f"Your letter gives {f['days']} days' notice ({doc}); our agreement provides for {c['days']} days ({ctr})."
        )
        return {"kind": "notice", "ids": [doc, ctr], "text": text, "strength": 5}

    def index_change(self, series):
        ids = self.ids(f"idx:{series}@")
        if not ids:

        m2 = ids[-1].split("@")[-1]
        m1 = months_back(m2, 12)

    def demo_refs(self):

        words = {

            "po": ("order_history", "We compared your offer with our recent order prices for this part ({ids}).", 4),
        }
        out = []
        for kind, (name, text, strength) in words.items():
            ids = [r for r in self.refs if r.startswith(f"{kind}:") and self.fact(r) is None]
            if ids:
                out.append(

        doc = self.case.get("trigger_doc")
        ctr = next((r for r in self.refs if r.startswith("ctr:")), None)
        if doc and ctr and self.fact(doc) is None and self.case.get("type") == "price_increase":

            out.append({"kind": "notice", "ids": [doc, ctr], "text": text, "strength": 5})
